behavior_items: The reproducer defines an inline helper `mpi_type_id(const unsigned long int*)` that simply returns `42`. This function is used as the initializer expression for a variable template, so each specialization computes an `int` value based on the type argument.

The variable template `template <typename T> const int mpi_type_id_for_type = mpi_type_id(static_cast<T*>(nullptr));` declares a namespace-scope `const` object for each specialization. Although the initializer always evaluates to `42` for `T = unsigned long`, the initializer is expressed as a function call, so the compiler is exercising its machinery for deciding whether the specialization is constant-initialized or instead emitted with dynamic initialization plus a guard.

The `broadcast()` function triggers an implicit instantiation by odr-using `mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long>`. That causes GCC to materialize the specialization before it later sees the explicit instantiation definition.

The later line `template const int mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long int>;` is an explicit instantiation definition of the same specialization. The reproducer specifically tests the compiler path where an explicit instantiation follows a prior implicit instantiation of a variable template specialization.

The bug report shows that this ordering matters: if only the implicit instantiation exists, only the explicit instantiation exists, or the explicit instantiation appears before `broadcast()`, the object is emitted correctly. Therefore the reproducer isolates a state-management bug in GCC's handling of already-instantiated variable-template metadata when an explicit instantiation definition arrives afterward.

For the failing case, GCC emits `mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long>` into `.rodata`, meaning it treats the variable object itself as read-only storage. At the same time, GCC also emits a guard variable in `.bss` and generates runtime static-initialization code that writes the computed value into the variable during startup.

Those two decisions are contradictory. A variable placed in `.rodata` must already be fully constant-initialized and never written at runtime, while the presence of a guard variable and a generated `__static_initialization_and_destruction_0` routine means GCC has decided the object requires dynamic initialization.

The disassembly in the report confirms the generated startup code: it sets the guard byte, calls `mpi_type_id`, then stores `%eax` into the address of `mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long>`. Because that address resolves into `.rodata`, the store faults at runtime and the program segfaults before `main` does anything meaningful.

The reproducer therefore exercises GCC's lowering of variable template specializations into ELF sections, especially the decision between writable zero-initialized storage such as `.bss` versus read-only constant storage such as `.rodata`. The correct behavior for an object that will be assigned during startup is to place it in writable storage.

The emitted symbol dump in the report shows exactly this mismatch: the specialization object is in `.rodata`, while its guard variable is in `.bss`. That combination strongly suggests GCC merged properties from two different compilation paths—one path classifying the specialization as a constant read-only object, another path generating dynamic initialization infrastructure.

The report also notes that changing the linkage spelling of the variable template (`inline`, `static`, `extern`) does not affect reproduction. That indicates the failure is not primarily about linkage semantics, but about the transition from implicit to explicit instantiation for a `const` variable template specialization.

Semantically, the reproducer is tiny, but it stresses a subtle corner of template instantiation bookkeeping: one specialization is first instantiated due to use in a function body, then explicitly instantiated later, and GCC must reconcile storage duration, section placement, constness, and initialization mode consistently. In the buggy versions, that reconciliation is inconsistent and produces a binary that is well-formed enough to link but invalid at runtime.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer targets GCC's handling of a `const` variable-template specialization that is implicitly instantiated by use and then explicitly instantiated later. GCC incorrectly classifies `mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long>` as read-only data and places it in `.rodata`, yet still emits dynamic static-initialization code and a guard variable that attempt to write the value at startup. This inconsistent combination causes the startup store into `.rodata` to segfault. The failure disappears when the explicit instantiation is removed or moved before the implicit use, showing the bug is specifically in GCC's state transition for explicit instantiation following prior implicit instantiation of the same variable-template specialization.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern is a contradiction in GCC's internal classification of the same variable-template specialization. `mpi_type_id_for_type<unsigned long>` is first implicitly instantiated by odr-use in `broadcast()`, then later explicitly instantiated. In the bad ordering only, GCC emits the object itself as read-only `.rodata` as if it were fully constant-initialized, but also emits a guard variable plus startup initialization code that calls `mpi_type_id` and stores into that object at runtime as if it required dynamic initialization. That means GCC is not consistently reconciling initialization kind, readonly-ness, and section placement when an explicit instantiation definition arrives after an existing implicit instantiation of a const variable template specialization. The bug is therefore most likely in C++ front-end template instantiation bookkeeping and/or varpool/assembler emission logic for namespace-scope const variable templates, where flags from the first instantiation path are retained while the later explicit-instantiation path adds dynamic initialization machinery without reclassifying storage as writable.

Mismatch between constant-initialization analysis and dynamic-initialization generation for variable templates: GCC may wrongly conclude the object is readonly because of `const`, while a separate path still generates guarded initialization for the same entity.

State caching bug for already-instantiated variable-template metadata keyed by specialization, where implicit instantiation records one storage/classification state and explicit instantiation later reuses that state instead of rebuilding it consistently.

Regression in handling of deferred/static initialization for templated namespace-scope variables, specifically the interaction among `const` qualification, COMDAT/weak emission, and guard-variable creation for explicit instantiation of an existing specialization.

related_methods.reason: Most suspicious because the bug is order-sensitive and specific to reconciling an existing implicit instantiation with a later explicit instantiation of the same variable-template specialization. This method registers a specialization of a template for given arguments and can return an equivalent prior declaration, so it is a natural place for stale specialization state, DECL flags, or metadata to be reused or merged incorrectly.

Highly suspicious because the failure depends on finding a previously created specialization when the explicit instantiation is later processed. This method retrieves an existing specialization for template arguments, so a bug here could cause GCC to reuse an earlier implicitly instantiated VAR_DECL without recomputing readonly/dynamic-initialization properties consistently.

This method is specifically for recording variable template instantiations, which is the exact entity involved in the bug. The failure is order-sensitive between implicit and later explicit instantiation, strongly suggesting broken bookkeeping or stale state for an already-instantiated variable template specialization.

This method determines DECL_EXTERNAL, DECL_COMDAT and related linkage/emission flags for VAR_DECLs. The bug looks like inconsistent final emission properties for the same specialization after explicit instantiation arrives, so a routine that finalizes object-file linkage and emission state is highly suspicious.

Most suspicious because the bug is explicitly order-sensitive and looks like a bad merge of state when an explicit instantiation definition arrives after an earlier implicit instantiation of the same variable-template specialization. This method is responsible for merging redeclarations, so it is a likely place for readonly/constant, initialization, or linkage flags to be combined inconsistently and leave the specialization classified as both dynamically initialized and read-only.

This method finishes variable declarations and installs initial values, making it a strong candidate for deciding whether a namespace-scope const variable specialization is constant-initialized or requires dynamic initialization. The failure shows contradictory treatment of the same decl, so a late explicit-instantiation path here could preserve an earlier readonly classification while also triggering static initialization machinery.

Most directly responsible for choosing the section for a VAR_DECL or CONST_DECL. The failure is exactly a wrong section-placement decision: the variable-template specialization is emitted in .rodata even though runtime initialization code later writes to it. A stale readonly/constant classification after implicit then explicit instantiation would likely surface here.

Central variable emission routine that coordinates how a variable is assembled, including whether it is treated as BSS/data/readonly and how definition-time properties are honored. An order-sensitive mismatch between dynamic initialization state and readonly emission could be exposed when this routine finalizes output for the specialization.

Most suspicious because the observed failure is wrong final emission of a variable specialization into .rodata instead of writable storage. This method is explicitly responsible for outputting a variable, so it is a prime place where stale readonly/initializer state could cause contradictory emission decisions after implicit then explicit instantiation.

Highly relevant because the bug is specifically about incorrect section placement versus initialization behavior. This method finalizes section-related flags and resolves section conflicts, so a failure to recompute or clear flags when the specialization changes from one instantiation state to another could leave the variable classified into a read-only section.

This method directly sets the section for a symbol node, which is highly relevant to the observed bug where the same variable-template specialization is emitted into .rodata instead of writable storage. The failure is specifically about inconsistent section placement after a later explicit instantiation changes initialization requirements, so a stale or incorrect section assignment here is very suspicious.

This overload copies section information from another node while maintaining section reference counts. The bug report strongly suggests properties from one symbol state/path are being merged into another inconsistently after implicit then explicit instantiation, and copying an outdated read-only section from another node would fit the .rodata/.bss mismatch well.

reviewed_methods.summary: Register the specialization SPEC as a specialization of TMPL with the indicated ARGS. IS_FRIEND indicates whether the specialization is actually just a friend declaration. ATTRLIST is the list of attributes that the specialization is declared with or NULL when it isn't. Returns SPEC, or an equivalent prior declaration, if available. We also store instantiations of field packs in the hash table, even though they are not themselves templates, to make lookup easier.
reviewed_methods.reason: Best match for the order-sensitive nature of the bug. The failure appears when a later explicit instantiation reuses an already implicitly instantiated variable-template specialization, and this routine is exactly where existing specializations are found, reused, and possibly merged. A stale or incompletely updated specialization entry here could easily preserve readonly/constant flags from one path while later logic adds dynamic initialization requirements.

reviewed_methods.signature: tree duplicate_decls (tree newdecl, tree olddecl, bool hiding, bool was_hidden)
reviewed_methods.summary: If NEWDECL is a redeclaration of OLDDECL, merge the declarations. If the redeclaration is invalid, a diagnostic is issued, and the error_mark_node is returned. Otherwise, OLDDECL is returned. If NEWDECL is not a redeclaration of OLDDECL, NULL_TREE is returned. HIDING is true if the new decl is being hidden. WAS_HIDDEN is true if the old decl was hidden. Hidden decls can be anticipated builtins, injected friends, or (coming soon) injected from a local-extern decl.
reviewed_methods.reason: Strong candidate because the reproducer depends on a later declaration of the same specialization changing behavior. If the explicit instantiation definition is merged into an existing implicit instantiation incorrectly, this is exactly the kind of routine that could leave conflicting flags in place: readonly/const placement from one declaration and dynamic-init requirements from another.

reviewed_methods.signature: void cp_finish_decl (tree decl, tree init, bool init_const_expr_p, tree asmspec_tree, int flags)
reviewed_methods.summary: Finish processing of a declaration; install its line number and initial value. If the length of an array type is not known before, it must be determined now, from the initial value, or it is an error. INIT is the initializer (if any) for DECL. If INIT_CONST_EXPR_P is true, then INIT is an integral constant expression. FLAGS is LOOKUP_ONLYCONVERTING if the = init syntax was used, else 0 if the (init) syntax was used.
reviewed_methods.reason: Likely involved because it finishes variable declarations and handles initializer-related properties, including whether a variable is treated as constant-initialized or needs runtime initialization. A late explicit-instantiation path could pass through here and fail to recompute storage mutability or initialization mode consistently for an already existing decl.

reviewed_methods.summary: Set section, do not recurse into aliases. When one wants to change section of a symbol and its aliases, use set_section.
reviewed_methods.reason: This method directly applies a specific section name to a symbol, so it is closely tied to the observed wrong placement of the variable-template specialization into .rodata. The bug symptoms suggest a stale readonly classification survives after later explicit instantiation adds dynamic initialization, and this setter is a plausible point where an old section assignment is preserved or not cleared/recomputed. It is slightly less than a perfect match because the deeper root cause may be earlier front-end state/flag computation rather than the low-level setter itself.

reviewed_methods.summary: Return the section into which the given VAR_DECL or CONST_DECL should be placed. PREFER_NOSWITCH_P is true if a noswitch section should be used wherever possible.
reviewed_methods.reason: This is the direct section-placement decision point, and the observable failure is exactly wrong placement into .rodata instead of writable storage. It is a strong fix location if the front end already sets inconsistent flags and this routine should defensively honor dynamic-initialization state over readonly classification; however, it may be only where the bad metadata becomes visible rather than where it originates.

reviewed_methods.signature: static tree retrieve_specialization (tree tmpl, tree args, hashval_t hash)
reviewed_methods.summary: Retrieve the specialization (in the sense of [temp.spec] - a specialization is either an instantiation or an explicit specialization) of TMPL for the given template ARGS. If there is no such specialization, return NULL_TREE. The ARGS are a vector of arguments, or a vector of vectors of arguments, in the case of templates with more than one level of parameters. If TMPL is a type template and CLASS_SPECIALIZATIONS_P is true, then we search for a partial specialization matching ARGS. This parameter is ignored if TMPL is not a class template. We can also look up a FIELD_DECL, if it is a lambda capture pack; the result is a NONTYPE_ARGUMENT_PACK.
reviewed_methods.reason: Very relevant because the explicit-instantiation path must find the earlier implicit specialization, and a bad lookup/reuse path could propagate stale state. However, this function mainly retrieves the prior decl rather than merging or updating its properties, so it is somewhat less likely than the registration/merge points to be the true fix location.

reviewed_methods.summary: Set the section of node THIS to be the same as the section of node OTHER. Keep reference counts of the sections up-to-date as needed.
reviewed_methods.reason: This overload copies section state from another symbol node, which fits the theory of inconsistent state merging between implicit and explicit instantiation paths. If the specialization inherits an outdated .rodata section from a prior node/state, this function could propagate the bad placement. However, it is somewhat less directly implicated than the string-based setter because the reproducer points more strongly to incorrect section classification/reclassification than to node-to-node copying specifically.

reviewed_methods.summary: Assemble everything that is needed for a variable or function declaration. Not used for automatic variables, and not used for function definitions. Should not be called for variables of incomplete structure type. TOP_LEVEL is nonzero if this variable has file scope. AT_END is nonzero if this is the special handling, at end of compilation, to define things that have had only tentative definitions. reviewed_methods.reason: Relevant final emission routine, but it mostly consumes previously established decl properties and calls get_variable_section. Unless the bug is in when or how it forces constructor/initializer state before emission, it seems more likely to expose the inconsistency than to create it.

If this function decides to place DECL in COMDAT, it will set appropriate flags -- but will not clear DECL_EXTERNAL. It is up to the caller to decide whether or not to clear DECL_EXTERNAL. Still, the reported symptom is more about initialization classification and section choice for the same specialization after redeclaration than about import/export linkage policy itself.
